newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's CEEE sells debentures for 214.2 mln reais.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's CEEE sells debentures for 214.2 mln reais.

text.p: Cia Estadual de Energia Eletrica (CEEE), a power firm owned by Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul state, on Thursday raked in 214.2 million reais ($199 million) from the sale of debentures on the Sao Paulo bolsa, officials said.
A bolsa spokesman said CEEE sold 40,000 simple debentures, which each had a nominal value of 5,000 reais, to 11 brokerages at a price of 5,354.58 reais a piece.
CEEE's goal in auctioning off the debentures was to replace expired and expiring short-term debt with long-term debt with a lower interest rate, officials said.
Bid specifications published Tuesday said the four-year debentures, which are not convertible to CEEE shares, will have an issue date of March 1, 1997.
The yield will be based on an initial spread of two percent on top of a local interbank reference rate known as ANBID, the company said.

Interest payments will be made semesterly over the first two years starting in September and amortization and interest rate payments will be made monthly for the last two years from March 1999 to February 2001, it added.
